answer: The network issues a cryptographic identity token stamped with a unique saffron‑colored hash that each agent must present to join a referral chain. When a recruiter invites a new node, the protocol checks the token against an ivory‑indexed ledger; any duplicate or overlapping prism‑derived signatures yield zero reward, forcing the recruiter to pay the full staking cost for each fresh identity. Thus a sybil attacker must acquire and lock up genuine tokens for every fake node, making the attack linearly expensive.
